content.text:
The restructuring is complete. Here's what I did and why.

## What I changed

**New collaborator: `EmailDomainClassifier`** (`rest/controller/EmailDomainClassifier.java`)
This codebase gives every cross-cutting concern its own small `@Component` collaborator — `TelephoneNormalizer`, `AddressNormalizer`, `CityRegionResolver`, `HouseholdResolver`. The email-domain concern was the odd one out: its disposable-domain table and domain-extraction lived inline inside `OwnerRegistrar`. I extracted it into a matching collaborator that owns:
- `DISPOSABLE_EMAIL_DOMAINS` (moved verbatim),
- `domainOf(email)` — the lower-cased domain (the inline `substring(indexOf('@')+1).toLowerCase(ROOT)`),
- `isDisposable(email)` — the existing exact-match rejection rule.

**`OwnerRegistrar`** now injects `EmailDomainClassifier` and calls `emailDomainClassifier.isDisposable(email)` instead of the inline set lookup. Behaviour is identical (the email is still syntactically validated first, still lower-cased on store).

## Why this is the right preparation

A direct implementation would cram `registrableBase` (domain parsing) and `hasDisposableAdjacentEmail` (disposable-adjacency) into `OwnerMapper` — a mapper has no business parsing domains. With `EmailDomainClassifier` now established as the home for email-domain knowledge, those two methods land there naturally next to `isDisposable`, and `riskFlag` becomes a thin three-way composition in `OwnerMapper` (the mapper already injects collaborators like `cityRegionResolver`/`telephoneNormalizer` the same way). The other two `riskFlag` inputs — `possibleDuplicate` and soft-capacity (`capacityWarning`) — are already stored booleans on `Owner`, so no prep was needed there.

I deliberately did **not** implement `riskFlag`/`registrableBase`/`hasDisposableAdjacentEmail`, or wire the classifier into `OwnerMapper` — that's the change itself.

The suite has exactly one `@Test`: `AcceptanceTest.coreRiskFlagFalseNormally`, which asserts `$.riskFlag == false`. ## What I changed

**New collaborator: `EmailDomainClassifier`** (`rest/controller/EmailDomainClassifier.java`)
This codebase gives every cross-cutting concern its own small `@Component` collaborator — `TelephoneNormalizer`, `AddressNormalizer`, `CityRegionResolver`, `HouseholdResolver`. The email-domain concern was the odd one out: its disposable-domain table and domain-extraction lived inline inside `OwnerRegistrar`. I extracted it into a matching collaborator that owns:
- `DISPOSABLE_EMAIL_DOMAINS` (moved verbatim),
- `domainOf(email)` — the lower-cased domain (the inline `substring(indexOf('@')+1).toLowerCase(ROOT)`),
- `isDisposable(email)` — the existing exact-match rejection rule.

**`OwnerRegistrar`** now injects `EmailDomainClassifier` and calls `emailDomainClassifier.isDisposable(email)` instead of the inline set lookup. Behaviour is identical (the email is still syntactically validated first, still lower-cased on store).

## Why this is the right preparation

A direct implementation would cram `registrableBase` (domain parsing) and `hasDisposableAdjacentEmail` (disposable-adjacency) into `OwnerMapper` — a mapper has no business parsing domains. With `EmailDomainClassifier` now established as the home for email-domain knowledge, those two methods land there naturally next to `isDisposable`, and `riskFlag` becomes a thin three-way composition in `OwnerMapper` (the mapper already injects collaborators like `cityRegionResolver`/`telephoneNormalizer` the same way). The other two `riskFlag` inputs — `possibleDuplicate` and soft-capacity (`capacityWarning`) — are already stored booleans on `Owner`, so no prep was needed there.

I deliberately did **not** implement `riskFlag`/`registrableBase`/`hasDisposableAdjacentEmail`, or wire the classifier into `OwnerMapper` — that's the change itself.
